title: SIU names man shot dead by Hamilton police
subtitle: Witness says she heard what sounded like gunshots; driver pulled unresponsive from van
article: The Ontario Special Investigations Unit has identified a man shot by Hamilton police Monday as Phonesay Chanthachak, 27.
The provincial agency said today Chanthachak, believed to be from Hamilton, was shot during "an interaction between HPS officers and Mr. Chanthachak" and an officer discharged his firearm.
Chanthachak was transported to Hamilton General Hospital, where he was pronounced dead.
An autopsy was scheduled for Tuesday in Hamilton.
Elementary and high school students cross the east-end street almost every day during lunch hour.

But within minutes Monday afternoon, Quigley Road near Albright Road became the taped-off scene of a Special Investigations Unit (SIU) probe into the death of a young man shot during a criminal investigation.
Parents in the area say they heard two "bangs" or "pops" just before 1 p.m. and saw a beige van mount the sidewalk and smash into a hydro pole.
The vehicle was immediately surrounded by unmarked police cars, and undercover officers ran over and took the male driver out of the van, said bystander Crystal Smith.

Smith says she realized the man was her 26-year-old friend, a Laotian called Pun. He was unresponsive even after police tried to resuscitate him through chest compressions on the sidewalk, said Smith, 23, as she stood at the intersection.
Police then placed him in an ambulance, she said, at which point she called the mother of the man's two young daughters.
"It all happened so fast."
Police said Tuesday Quigley Road at Albright remains closed for the ongoing SIU and Hamilton police investigation.
Road closures from yesterday remain in effect.
Students from Bishop Ryan school will have access on to Quigley from King Street East. There is no further public access other than students.
Students from Sir Willfred Laurier will have access on to Albright from Mount Albion Road.

Police are not saying much about the events leading up to the crash, which forced traffic to be rerouted from the school zone for hours. The SIU will only say Hamilton police were conducting a "criminal investigation" in the area in which there was an "interaction" between officers and the man.
The man was shot during this interaction and pronounced dead at Hamilton General Hospital, according to the SIU.
SIU spokesperson Jasbir Brar said the agency has assigned seven investigators and three forensic investigators to probe the circumstances of the incident.
Hamilton police refused to comment further, citing the involvement of the SIU.
"All I can say is that it was a criminal investigation," Sergeant Terri-Lynn Collings said.
Schools in the area were advised of the situation, but there were no public safety concerns, she said.
But another witness, who would only give her first name, Julie, said she was nervous about the incident occurring so close to children.
"You might be doing a chase, but what if there are kids on the street?" said the 27-year-old mother of two.
Julie said she saw four or five undercover officers run out of their vehicles after the van crashed into the pole.
The investigation scene is within walking distance of Bishop Ryan Catholic Secondary and Sir Wilfrid Laurier Elementary schools.
At least two bullet holes were visible through the front window of the van at the scene. The airbag had deployed and there was blood on the bag and driver's seat. A passenger side window was missing.
Six other vehicles were within the area bounded by police tape.
Smith said Pun, whose last name she doesn't know, "was on the run" and in trouble with police, but she didn't know what the situation was.
"I know him. He's not the type to have a gun. He's a really good dad," she said.
The SIU investigates reports involving police where there has been death, serious injury or allegations of sexual assault.
